title: [storage] The scratch walk collects a large root within its bound: a leased claim is walked by its build paths only, a fresh or running entry stops early, a session folder's other children are each their own entry, scratch_bound is configurable, a root inside a root (/data/tmp/ccd) is its own, and an exclude above a root is refused out loud
prompt:
Spawn, objective 155 [storage] (projects-47, 2026-11-14: "(a), (b) and (c); (d) by configuration"; reviewer rev-g): the storage line's scratch walk collects a large root within its bound. Today live's walk of /data/tmp runs over it (serve's log 06:31: "the walk of /data/tmp ran over its bound (1000000 entries, 5000 ms); the previous figure is kept"), so "scratch nobody owns" is never collected there, which is what 140 exists to collect. With /data/tmp/ccd made a root of its own, each session folder (rev-b-tmp, rev-f-123, …) is an entry with its owner and age: the owner's "an owner and age per folder" (187 GB went unseen this way).

R2 (rev-g's FIX on R1 d85f5eae, F1 and F2 in 155.sh only; projects-47 on rev-g's notes, 2026-11-14: "take (a) in R2 ... add a scenario check"; "(b) ... refuse it loudly ... include it"):
- F1: 155.sh's (2) also reads with roots [N, N/ccd] and no exclude (inner-root-counted survived the scenario: only a unit test caught it).
- F2 and the lead's (a): a session folder (an unmarked, unclaimed directory holding a running claim one level below) is no entry itself, and each of its other children is judged as an entry of its own (owner, gone, idle, fresh, lease ended), so one claim hides none of its unclaimed siblings (R1 made the whole folder someone's: rev-b-tmp's one claim would have hidden its unclaimed children, the blind spot of the 187 GB). 155.sh's (1) adds sess/ with a leased sess/o and an unclaimed, old sess/old-tree.
- The lead's (b): an exclude that holds a root refuses that root, named in the answer and not collected, never a silent nothing. New 155.sh check (6).
- 155.sh empties serve.log before each start (its port read could see the last serve's port: R2 starts serve five times, and one run hit it).

Why. Measured 2026-11-14 (find, read only): /data/tmp holds 1,346,093 entries, 913k of them under ccd (ccd/rev-b-tmp 349k, ccd/rev-e-tmp 335k, both claimed). find takes 12.6 s over them. scratch.rs's walk_in walks every top-level entry whole (bytes, newest change, *.jsonl), claimed folders included, then their build paths a second time. /data/tmp/ccd is one top-level entry, so all of it is walked every 10 minutes to learn that something in it changed today.

Read first: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/scratch.rs (walk_in, found, claimed, claimed_below, related, the tests), unowned.rs (settings, Plan, read, the cache), web/src/coreLines.ts (scratchMark), docs/storage.md (the storage line's two read-only guardrails).

What changes (scratch.rs, unowned.rs, coreLines.ts, docs/storage.md). What is counted does not change, except one double count removed (below):
(a) A folder whose claim's lease runs is someone's and never walked whole: its build paths only. Its `bytes` in the answer is null (`Claimed.bytes: Option<u64>`), its `build_bytes` as before. A claimed folder whose lease has ended is walked whole, as before: it is a nobody-owns candidate.
(b) An entry whose marker's process runs is never walked (it is someone's). An unmarked, unclaimed entry's walk stops at its first change in the last 24 h (`found(…, recent_after)`): it is its maker's, and its bytes and *.jsonl are never needed. Gone and idle entries, and ended leases, are walked whole as before.
    An unmarked, unclaimed directory holding a claim whose lease runs one level below is a session folder (R2): it is no entry itself, and each of its children is judged as an entry of its own, by the same rules as a root's entries (a claimed child: owned while its lease runs, lease ended after; an unclaimed one: gone, fresh or idle). Before 155 the folder could be counted idle with that claim's bytes inside, while the claim was listed beside it: the same bytes twice. In R1 it was someone's whole, which hid its unclaimed children. Finding a session folder reads the claim files one level down only; nothing is walked for it.
(c) The Core lines file's `"storage": {"scratch_bound": {"entries": <n>, "ms": <n>}}` sets each root's bound (both whole numbers from 1; otherwise the default, 1,000,000 entries / 5 s). It is carried in the Plan, so a change in the file starts a new reading.
(d) A root inside another root (projects-47: /data/tmp/ccd beside /data/tmp) is walked as its own, each of its folders an entry with its own owner and age:
    - The outer root's walk skips an entry that is, or holds, another configured root, so nothing is counted twice even without an exclude.
    - An exclude that is a root itself is for the roots around it, not for its own walk. Before 155, related() matched both ways, so with roots [/data/tmp, /data/tmp/ccd] and exclude [/data/tmp/ccd] every entry of the ccd root lay under the exclude and the ccd root counted nothing, silently.
    - An exclude that holds a root (an ancestor: exclude [/data/tmp] with root /data/tmp/ccd) refuses that root (R2, the lead's (b)): the answer's scratch.refused names it, "exclude <X> hides root <Y>: a root under an exclude is never read", serve's log says it, and the figure is not collected while it stands (as for a root refused through a symlink). Never a silent nothing.
    - Excludes inside the inner root still hold.
(e) The card (coreLines.ts scratchMark): a leased folder reads "build <size> (not walked whole while leased) · <age> old · lease until … · …"; a folder with bytes as before.
(f) docs/storage.md: the four rules, `scratch_bound`, and the live file's line. The live file is a lead step: `scratch_roots` ["/var/tmp/spawn", "/data/tmp", "/data/tmp/ccd"], `scratch_exclude` ["/var/tmp/spawn/sync", "/data/tmp/ccd"]. The old line said ["/var/tmp/spawn"], but live's file already had /data/tmp.
The refactors are moves, there to keep functions under clippy's 100 lines: `left_out()` (the leave-out conditions), and in R2 `Judging` (one root's walk in progress: `entries_of`, the loop over a directory's entries, and `judge`, the per-entry rules walk_in had inline), so a session folder's children go through the same rules as a root's entries. `refused_roots` takes the excludes.

Never changed: read only (nothing removed, moved or touched); symlinks never followed; the fixed exclusions and NEVER; a root refused through a symlink; a walk past its bound keeps the previous figure, never a partial count; 140's claim file, its CLI and the listing's order.

Tests (unit, scratch.rs): a_running_lease_and_a_fresh_folder_are_never_walked_whole (a root that fits 60 entries only because a leased folder is walked by its build path and a fresh one stops at its own time; with the lease ended, the same root runs over the bound); a_root_inside_a_root_is_its_own_and_counted_once (roots /x and /x/ccd, with and without the exclude: /x/b, /x/ccd/a and /x/ccd/c each once; an exclude inside the inner root holds). a_session_folder_hides_none_of_its_unclaimed_children (R2: sess holding a leased sess/o; its children old-tree, loose (a file), gone (a dead marker), ended (a lease ended) are each their own entry, fresh is not, sess is none); an_exclude_above_a_root_refuses_it_and_says_so (R2: the words, nothing counted, an exclude equal to the root refuses nothing). a_claim_is_owned_while_its_lease_runs_and_listed_by_owner now expects bytes None for leased folders, no "old" entry (it holds a running claim), and old/data as its own idle entry (R2). web/test/coreLines.test.ts: the leased folder's words.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/scratch.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/unowned.rs, web/src/coreLines.ts, web/test/coreLines.test.ts, docs/storage.md, rsi/scenarios/155.sh (new), rsi/scenarios/140.sh (a kept edit, below). The fleet's part touches no path in rsi/scenarios/protected (web/src and web/test are allowed); 155.sh and the 140.sh edit ship with the contract. 159 (rev-g) also touches web/src/coreLines.ts, web/test/coreLines.test.ts and docs/storage.md and is stacked after 155 (sync/obj-155/NOTE-159.txt: the R1 stack passed on e45ad3c0).
Size (R2, measured from the compiled diff, 10e12924 against live main 9623b066): code +283 −93 (scratch.rs +251 −88, much of it the move into Judging; unowned.rs +24 −3; coreLines.ts +8 −2); tests +256 −9; docs +30 −4. Under the 300-line rule. R2 alone on R1 (d85f5eae..10e12924): scratch.rs +292 −97 (code and tests), unowned.rs +3 −2, docs +8 −4.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/155.sh, black box, its own database, a scratch HOME, `spawn serve` on 127.0.0.1:0 with a Core lines file under its workspace root:
(1) with scratch_bound {entries 900, ms 30000}, a root holding a claimed folder whose lease runs (2000 files, a 3000-byte target/), an unmarked folder changed now (2000 files), an idle one (600 bytes, 2 days old), and an unmarked session folder sess (2 days old) holding sess/o (claimed, its lease running, 500 bytes) and sess/old-tree (unclaimed, 1000 bytes): storage.unowned_scratch_bytes is 1600, scratch.unowned is idle and sess/old-tree (sess is no entry), scratch.claimed is the leased folder (bytes null, build_bytes 3000) and sess/o (bytes null, build_bytes 0);
(2) roots [N, N/ccd], with exclude [N/ccd] and again with no exclude: scratch.unowned is N/ccd/x (7), N/ccd/y (11) and N/top (50), each once; the figure is 68;
(3) scratch_bound {entries 5}: the figure is null and serve's log says "ran over its bound (5 entries";
(4) the card's words for the leased folder: "build <size> (not walked whole while leased) · … old · lease until …";
(5) nothing under the scratch changed;
(6) roots [N/ccd], exclude [N]: the figure is null and scratch.refused is [{"root": N/ccd, "why": "exclude N hides root N/ccd: a root under an exclude is never read"}].
rsi/scenarios/140.sh, a kept edit (as 152 carried 149.sh): its (2) expects bytes null for the two leased folders (a, sess/o) and its (4) the leased folder's new words. The reviewed 140.sh still passes on the base, and the edited one on the throwaway.

Proof (rev-e, R2: throwaway 10e12924 on live main 9623b066, base tree 9623b066; run-155r2.sh -> /data/tmp/ccd/rev-e-tmp/s155out3, then run-155r2b.sh -> s155out3b after the serve.log fix):
- 155.sh on the base: exit 1. It fails (1), with sess counted whole and old-tree inside it, and the leased folder's bytes not null; (2), where the inner root counts nothing with the exclude (50, not 68) and twice without it (86); (3), where scratch_bound is ignored (2207, not null) and the log says nothing; (4), the card's words; and (6), where the hidden root counts 0 silently and nothing is refused.
- On the throwaway, 155.sh exits 0 three times (s155out3b) and once in s155out3. s155out3's first throwaway run exited 2: a harness error, GET answered 000. A start_serve read the previous serve's port from serve.log before the new process's redirect had truncated it. 155.sh now empties serve.log before each start; the three passing runs are with that fix.
- Kept edit: the reviewed 140.sh passes on the base and fails on the throwaway, as expected. The edited 140.sh passes on the throwaway, in s155out3 and again in s155out3b. 094.sh and 141.sh pass on the throwaway.
- `cargo test -p spawn-cli -- --list` against the base: 0 missing, 4 new: a_running_lease_and_a_fresh_folder_are_never_walked_whole, a_root_inside_a_root_is_its_own_and_counted_once, a_session_folder_hides_none_of_its_unclaimed_children, an_exclude_above_a_root_refuses_it_and_says_so.
- fmt --check and clippy -D warnings are clean. The core_lines unit tests pass (61). Web tests: 21 pass, 0 fail.
- Mutants (mut-155.py R2, each applied alone): 11 of 11 killed, each by a 155.sh check and most by a unit test too. The tree is clean after.
  leased-walked, leased-top-walked: (1), plus the claim test, the session-folder test and the running-lease test;
  no-early-stop: (1), plus the running-lease test;
  held-not-owned (the session folder judged whole): (1), plus the claim test and the session-folder test;
  siblings-hidden (R1's rule: the session folder someone's whole): (1), plus the claim test and the session-folder test;
  inner-root-counted: (2) without the exclude (F1), plus the nested-root test;
  exclude-own-root: (2) with the exclude, plus the nested-root test;
  ancestor-exclude-silent: (6), plus the exclude-above test;
  bound-ignored: (3);
  card-shows-zero: (4), plus the web test.
- The mutant runs used the 155.sh from before the serve.log fix. Every mutant failed on assertions (blackbox lines), none on a harness exit.
- R1's proof (r1/155-proof.txt, s155out2): 8 of 8 killed; inner-root-counted and held-not-owned only by unit tests (rev-g's F1 and F2).

Verified by (projects-47, after the landing and the deploy, then the live file's roots and exclude as in (f)):
- the Home card's Storage row shows each /data/tmp/ccd session folder with its owner (claimed) or among "nobody owns" with its age;
- storage.unowned_scratch_bytes is collected (not null) at two readings 10 minutes apart, and serve's log has no "ran over its bound" for /data/tmp or /data/tmp/ccd between them.
